heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 Mini runs Polymaker PolyTerra PLA flawlessly out of the box with its stock stainless steel nozzle and open-frame design. Leveraging an effective volumetric flow rate of 21 mm³/s, the setup achieves reliable print speeds of up to 250 mm/s at standard layer heights without hardware modifications.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate clean with dish soap and warm water (no adhesive required)
slicerTweaks: Set Max Volumetric Speed to 21 mm³/s in the Filament Settings to unlock print speeds up to 250 mm/s safely.
Configure Pressure Advance (PA) to approximately 0.024 in OrcaSlicer to compensate for the higher elasticity of matte PLA additives.
Set Nozzle Temperature to 210°C (215°C for first layer) and Heated Bed to 55°C for consistent inter-layer bonding without inducing heat creep.
Lower outer wall acceleration to 3000 mm/s² and outer wall speed to 120 mm/s to ensure a uniform matte surface finish devoid of gloss banding.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Weak Z-axis layer adhesion or brittle parts
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PolyTerra contains organic/mineral matte additives that lower tensile layer bonding at high linear printing speeds when overcooled.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Increase nozzle temperature by 5-10°C (up to 220°C) and reduce maximum part cooling fan from 100% to 70% in OrcaSlicer cooling settings.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Under-extrusion at high speeds or fast infill
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Volumetric flow bottleneck through the stock stainless steel nozzle exceeding the melt rate at rapid linear velocities.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Hard cap the OrcaSlicer 'Max volumetric speed' parameter to 21 mm³/s and lower sparse infill speeds from 300 mm/s to 250 mm/s.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: First layer peeling or corner warping
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Oils and residue on the Textured PEI surface combined with slight thermal contraction on an open bed.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Scrub the PEI sheet with warm water and basic dish soap, dry thoroughly, and set first layer bed temperature to 60°C with fan speed off for the first 3 layers.

faq.question: Does Polymaker PolyTerra PLA require a hardened steel nozzle on the A1 Mini?
faq.answer: No. PolyTerra PLA uses non-abrasive organic and mineral fillers rather than glass or carbon fiber, making the stock A1 Mini stainless steel nozzle completely suitable for long-term printing.

faq.question: Can I use PolyTerra PLA cardboard spools in the Bambu Lab AMS Lite?
faq.answer: Yes, but cardboard edges can generate paper dust or slip on the AMS Lite rotary rollers. It is highly recommended to print and press-fit a reusable rim adapter or apply electrical tape along the spool edge.

faq.question: Why do some areas of my PolyTerra print look glossy while others look matte?
faq.answer: Matte finish in PolyTerra PLA is strongly dependent on printing speed and temperature; slower print paths allow more heat absorption and become glossy. Enforce uniform outer wall speeds (e.g., 100-120 mm/s) across all geometries in OrcaSlicer.

faq.question: Do I need to enclose the Bambu Lab A1 Mini to print PolyTerra PLA?
faq.answer: No, an enclosure is actually detrimental when printing PLA. The A1 Mini open-bed design promotes optimal heat dissipation and prevents cold-end heat creep clogs.
